## Scope and evidence

Read-only review completed for `MS-LIFETIME-AUTHORITY.T5`.

Read the canonical instructions, exact Burn issue, combined decision, and AIMeter source at `c842efc`. Reap started at `2df8545`. No files, tracking records, agents, databases, or runtime state changed.

**Conclusion:** Permanent archives need provider-specific preservation and restoration gates. A verified file copy alone cannot authorize source removal.

## Provider/consumer inventory

| Component | Existing evidence | Required design treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Codex native history | AIMeter discovers both `sessions` and `archived_sessions`. It canonicalizes and deduplicates their targets. [paths.rs](/Users/spencer/src/aimeter/crates/aimeter-core/src/paths.rs:347) | Capture active and archived history, descendants, native IDs, related files, and required database state. Do not treat native archive state as external preservation. |
| Codex databases | AIMeter names `state_5.sqlite` and `logs_2.sqlite`. Its account documentation describes a shared session index. These sources do **not** establish the complete current history-database set. [paths.rs](/Users/spencer/src/aimeter/crates/aimeter-core/src/paths.rs:104), [account plan](/Users/spencer/src/aimeter/docs/plans/multi-codex-account.md:94) | Require a version-specific inventory. Classify each database as required history, required metadata, or unrelated diagnostic data. Do not infer completeness from filename patterns. |
| Claude native history | AIMeter recursively reads `projects/**/*.jsonl`, with cycle protection for directory aliases. [claude.rs](/Users/spencer/src/aimeter/crates/aimeter-core/src/claude.rs:921) | Preserve the parent transcript and its descendant tree. Claude documents separate subagent transcripts and `.meta.json` sidecars. [Claude subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents) |
| Claude related files | Claude documents checkpoint files under `file-history`, attachments under `uploads`, and some session data under temporary storage. `history.jsonl` supports prompt recall, not full conversation recovery. [Claude directory](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory) | Capture required session dependencies outside `projects`. Distinguish conversation restoration from checkpoint restoration. Do not silently omit referenced content because it lies outside the transcript directory. |
| Shared homes | Codex session roots and Claude project roots can be shared. Account discovery and history discovery have different boundaries. [paths.rs](/Users/spencer/src/aimeter/crates/aimeter-core/src/paths.rs:214), [account discovery](/Users/spencer/src/aimeter/crates/aimeter-core/src/codex_accounts.rs:128) | Store each shared payload once. Record alias relationships separately. Retrieval must reconstruct archive-local relationships without live absolute symlinks. |
| AIMeter | Cursors use provider/path keys. Native context, event IDs, execution origin, and repair evidence have separate roles. [db.rs](/Users/spencer/src/aimeter/crates/aimeter-core/src/db.rs:1862), [native correction design](/Users/spencer/src/aimeter/docs/design/native-usage-corrections.md:54) | Keep archives outside routine discovery. Preserve source paths and native identities as evidence; do not convert archive placement into execution ownership. |

## Strongest failure traces

### 1. Successful Codex archive, missing child

`thread/archive(parent)` succeeds → one descendant cannot archive → caller accepts success → source cleanup removes an incomplete tree.

Official documentation expressly permits this result. Default thread listings also omit archived and non-interactive sources. Require explicit discovery coverage and a per-descendant inventory, not one successful parent response. Current history can require pagination; metadata alone is insufficient. [Codex App Server](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server)

**Minimum mechanism:** A version-specific closure inventory, with explicit unresolved descendants and capture boundaries.

### 2. Consistent database, inconsistent conversation

Transcript captured at boundary A → history database captured at boundary B → a concurrent append, fork, or deletion occurs between them.

SQLite backup establishes database consistency, not consistency across multiple databases and transcript files. Completion requires `sqlite3_backup_step()` to reach `SQLITE_DONE`; `sqlite3_backup_finish() == SQLITE_OK` alone is insufficient. External writes can restart backup progress. [SQLite backup contract](https://sqlite.org/c3ref/backup_finish.html)

**Minimum mechanism:** A provider-supported capture boundary, or a demonstrated equivalent that covers the complete dependency set. Bound retries. If consistency remains unknown, retain the source.

### 3. Quiet observation, late append, source deletion

Capture verifies length L → an idle session resumes and appends → cleanup unlinks the source → the archive lacks the final records.

Repeated size/mtime observations do not prevent this race. Reap reservations cannot exclude independent provider writers.

**Minimum mechanism:** A proven provider-coordinated removal boundary. Without one, permit preservation copies but block source removal. Never stop agents or editors.

### 4. Export succeeds, native restoration fails

Codex `/export` produces Markdown and requires the current turn to finish. Its documentation does not establish native import from that export. [Developer commands](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/developer-commands)

Claude `/export` produces readable text. Claude also documents resume from an absolute JSONL transcript path, but its internal entry format changes between versions. That does not prove complete descendant, attachment, or checkpoint restoration. [Claude sessions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions)

**Minimum mechanism:** Record provider version, storage format, supported restore procedure, and demonstrated limits. Prove retrieval and native restoration without original homes or Reap state. Do not require private database or transcript edits without a demonstrated safe interface.

### 5. Verified archive, permanently missed AIMeter tail

AIMeter commits offset O → provider writes through L → archive preserves L → source disappears before AIMeter consumes O…L.

Both collectors bound reads to an observed file length and defer incomplete trailing lines. Codex can skip absent files; disappearance is not evidence that all usage was consumed. [codex.rs](/Users/spencer/src/aimeter/crates/aimeter-core/src/codex.rs:945), [claude.rs](/Users/spencer/src/aimeter/crates/aimeter-core/src/claude.rs:728)

**Minimum mechanism:** Before removal, require an origin-owned acknowledgement through the exact final capture boundary, including deferred completion records. No such archive acknowledgement interface was established by this review. It is a future capability, not an existing guarantee.

### 6. Retrieval becomes duplicate consumption

A previously consumed file appears under a new discovered path → its cursor starts at zero → fallback event keys change → old usage can enter again.

Codex fallback keys include path and scan-fragment identity. Claude falls back to path plus record offset when native identifiers are absent. Preserve filenames too: Codex’s collector derives its stored `session_id` from the filename stem. [Codex keys](/Users/spencer/src/aimeter/crates/aimeter-core/src/codex.rs:1206), [filename identity](/Users/spencer/src/aimeter/crates/aimeter-core/src/codex.rs:2132), [Claude keys](/Users/spencer/src/aimeter/crates/aimeter-core/src/claude.rs:790)

**Minimum mechanism:** Archive extraction stays outside discovery. Native restoration needs explicit replay controls before a restored tree becomes visible to AIMeter. Never reset ingestion cursors as an archive operation.

### 7. Archive host becomes execution origin

Laptop history is restored on the mini → collection treats it as new local evidence → historical ownership or corrections acquire the wrong origin.

Native metadata repair and completion repair explicitly require the execution origin. Gateway lineage also rejects conflicting, truncated, or remote-proxy evidence. [metadata guard](/Users/spencer/src/aimeter/crates/aimeter-core/src/attribution.rs:337), [completion guard](/Users/spencer/src/aimeter/crates/aimeter-core/src/native_repair.rs:239), [lineage guard](/Users/spencer/src/aimeter/crates/aimeter-core/src/agent_lineage.rs:183)

**Minimum mechanism:** Preserve source host, native IDs, original paths, and existing account/project/parent evidence. Keep unknown attribution unknown. Archive location and current login grant no historical ownership.

## Minimum integrated requirement

Use one archive manifest and the existing executor/journal. Add these provider/consumer gates:

1. **Closure:** Exact payloads, descendants, dependencies, aliases, versions, and unresolved items.
2. **Capture:** Consistent database state and an explicit cross-file boundary.
3. **Preservation:** Verified destination identity, durable publication, integrity evidence, and permanent retention.
4. **Consumption:** Origin-owned AIMeter acknowledgement through the removal boundary.
5. **Removal:** Fresh source identity, unchanged closure, and protection against late provider writes.
6. **Retrieval:** Native restoration and replay controls independent of original homes and Reap state.

A missing gate must block source removal without blocking independent preservation work. Permanent payloads must never enter quarantine expiry or generic job-output cleanup.

**No runtime completeness, native restoration, or unchanged AIMeter claim is established here.** These are requirements and failure traces for the integrated draft.

## First review: required integration

Read the exact issue, canonical `AGENTS.md`, full design, prior red-team proof, and relevant source at `2df8545`. No files or tracker records changed.

**Conclusion:** Permanent archive must be a core preservation operation, not quarantine with a hold. Reuse the coordinator, admission protocol, reservations, and recovery journal.

### Requirements and adversarial traces

| Requirement | Concrete trace | Minimum design response |
|---|---|---|
| **Separate archive and prune authority** | A size threshold starts archival. The transfer succeeds, then generic move completion deletes the source without separate consent. | Co-located opt-in archive policy can coexist with KEEP. Define size accounting, threshold, and eligibility without numeric defaults. Source pruning requires separate explicit authority. Unmet eligibility leaves the source over budget. |
| **Permanent protection across every cleanup path** | A copied archive contains expired `.reap` files or Cargo markers. Alternatively, quarantine configuration points above the archive, followed by `purge --all`. | Give archive roots a durable preservation role, outside state and quarantine. Every destructive executor must reject units inside, containing, or overlapping that role. Include Cargo, stores, declarations, leases, purge selectors, orphan cleanup, and recovery cleanup. Ordinary selectors never grant archive deletion authority. |
| **Verified destination identity** | `/Volumes/kytos` disappears. Directory creation writes onto the mini’s internal disk. A different volume later occupies the same pathname. | Bind `/Volumes/kytos/backups/agent-conversations` to the verified volume and root identity. Reject absent, substituted, ambiguous, or symlinked destinations. Revalidate through transfer and commit; never create a fallback mountpoint. Reject source/destination overlap. |
| **Durable remote commit** | The mini publishes an archive, but the acknowledgement is lost. The laptop retries, receives “unknown,” and creates another capture or prunes prematurely. | Use a stable capture identity and exact payload digest. The receiver durably publishes verified payload, manifest, and commit evidence before acknowledgement. Same identity/content returns the existing result; different content conflicts. Unknown acceptance preserves the source and requires reconciliation. |
| **Recovery without local Reap state** | Local jobs, epochs, and caches disappear after remote commit. A new installation repeats the capture or cannot establish preservation. | Preserve capture identity, inventory, integrity evidence, and commit evidence with the archive. Remote lookup must survive local job-record expiry. State loss cannot authorize source pruning or replay with fresh intent. Uncertain staging remains protected until reconciled. |
| **Independent discovery and retrieval** | Both original homes disappear. The owner knows a conversation ID but has no Reap database. | Preserve the requested host/provider/archive layout and native relative paths. Readable manifests locate conversations, descendants, capture boundaries, and integrity evidence. Discovery uses archive manifests, not transcript parsing or an indispensable central catalog. Standard extraction must suffice for compressed payloads. |
| **One payload for shared aliases** | Two account aliases expose the same session directory. Separate jobs archive it twice and later prune incompatible logical views. | Resolve shared physical sources before work admission. Capture shared history once; record alias relationships separately. Archive references remain internal and relative. Preserve historical attribution; unknown ownership stays unknown. Avoid a general deduplication service. |
| **Safe capture and source pruning** | A session appends after capture. A database snapshot is internally valid but disagrees with associated conversation files. A path is replaced before deletion. | Define the complete capture boundary and eligible prune units. Pruning requires verified preservation, current explicit consent, unchanged source identity/content, and provider-safe removal. Quiet time or absent open handles alone cannot prove this. If writers cannot be excluded safely, retain the source; never stop agents or editors. |
| **Shared reservations and concurrent edits** | Cleanup removes a source during transfer. A second host publishes the same archive slot. An owner edits the source after verification. | Reserve source dependency closure, destination slot, and affected database/alias resources through existing executors on both hosts. Acquire complete conflict sets without deadlock. Retain exclusions through uncertain effects. Revalidate before prune. State the existing raw-edit race limit; do not claim atomicity against arbitrary writers. |
| **Bounded useful work** | An active home remains above threshold. Each maintenance pass reparses its entire history, launches compression helpers, and retransmits unchanged captures. | Reuse bounded workers, streaming, helper limits, staging limits, and fair safe-unit quanta. Coalesce compatible pending captures. Use rebuildable progress hints and durable capture evidence to avoid repeat work. Bound compression concurrency and network buffering. Capacity exhaustion preserves sources. No runtime CPU governor is required. |
| **Credential and path safety** | A broad home copy includes credentials. A manifest path contains `../`; a native symlink escapes into another home. | Use provider-specific capture inventories. Exclude credential files and unrelated caches/executables by default. Validate archive components, extraction paths, links, file types, and containment. Do not execute manifest text or follow absolute source links. Unsupported layouts block completeness and prune claims. |
| **Explicit migration and honest disk effects** | Existing external histories are merely relabelled as archives. Same-volume relocation is reported as freed space or an independent backup. | Inventory, verify, and import existing histories into the same archive shape. Do not activate policy or remove originals through metadata conversion. Report source reduction, archive allocation, staging peak, and actual per-volume effects separately. One external disk is not an independent second backup. |

### Source-derived constraints

- [Explicit purge selection](/Users/spencer/src/reap/src/quarantine.rs:915) bypasses holds and automatic grace. A quarantine hold cannot establish permanence.
- [Directory movement](/Users/spencer/src/reap/src/util.rs:157) couples preservation and source removal. Its cross-volume verification compares counts and bytes, not content integrity. It is not an archive commit primitive.
- [Declaration removal guards](/Users/spencer/src/reap/src/files.rs:245) protect quarantine overlap, not permanent archive roles.
- [The current design](/Users/spencer/src/reap/docs/decisions/DEC-LIFETIME-AUTHORITY.md:62) allows Cargo compaction under workspace KEEP. Therefore, ordinary sealed KEEP alone is insufficient archive protection.

### Missing mechanisms versus future proof

**Required design additions:** archive/prune authority split; durable archive role; receiver commit/replay semantics; state-loss recovery; retrieval layout; cross-host reservations; migration rules; resource and disk accounting.

**Future implementation gates:** fault injection at each transfer/publication/prune boundary; lost acknowledgements and local-state loss; volume substitution; concurrent writers and cleanup; every ordinary deletion entry point; bounded-resource measurements; retrieval without original homes.

Provider-native restoration, capture consistency, descendants, and unchanged AIMeter behavior remain mandatory acceptance gates. The other reviewer owns their detailed evidence.

**The first identity capability gate remains open and unchanged.** No archive receipt, checksum, or transfer success substitutes for the required non-reuse/generation capability. Missing capability still blocks disposal adoption and conversion.

This is the first requirements review, not acceptance of an integrated design. Parent synthesis, full-draft rereview, and final acceptance remain separate.

## Round-2 result

Read all 1,001 lines. The SHA-256 matches the supplied value.

**One high finding remains.** One medium contradiction also needs correction. No changes or experiments were made.

### 1. High — Shared external source protection lacks reverse discovery

**Sections:** 6A, 9, 10, 11. See [source veto](/Users/spencer/src/reap/docs/decisions/DEC-LIFETIME-AUTHORITY.md:301), [discovery](/Users/spencer/src/reap/docs/decisions/DEC-LIFETIME-AUTHORITY.md:719), and [profile scope](/Users/spencer/src/reap/docs/decisions/DEC-LIFETIME-AUTHORITY.md:845).

**Trace:**

1. A home has `conversation_source` policy and links `sessions` to an external history directory.
2. A generic cleanup selects that external directory or its ancestor.
3. Its ancestor/descendant scan cannot find the declaration in the separate home.
4. No archive role or archive-endpoint binding covers this source directory.
5. The stated discovery method can therefore miss the source-release obligation.

The draft requires the veto but does not explain how a destructive operation discovers this inbound dependency. Canonical deduplication during capture does not solve reverse discovery during independent cleanup.

**Minimum correction:** Establish protection at every canonical external history component before activation. Either:

- Put effective co-located protection at those components; or
- Define an explicit profile binding that destructive operations consult by canonical identity.

For a binding, specify policy-generation validation, restart/configuration-loss behavior, and conflict invalidation. It must route to source policy, not become another lifetime database.

**Decisive acceptance proof:** Declare the policy only at the home, with history on an external target. Select the target and its ancestor through generic deletion, stores, legacy retirement, purge where applicable, and Cargo where applicable. All must refuse without a native-prune transaction. Repeat after restart, cache loss, alias replacement, and unavailable source-policy reads.

This is a discovery-mechanism gap, not a missing future provider capability.

### 2. Medium — Attribution ambiguity both blocks and permits complete preservation

**Section:** 6A. [Line 326](/Users/spencer/src/reap/docs/decisions/DEC-LIFETIME-AUTHORITY.md:326) conflicts with [line 385](/Users/spencer/src/reap/docs/decisions/DEC-LIFETIME-AUTHORITY.md:385).

**Trace:**

1. A conversation has a complete native closure and a valid capture boundary.
2. Historical account evidence is absent or conflicting.
3. Line 326 blocks completeness because attribution is ambiguous.
4. Line 385 and the issue require unknown attribution to remain unknown.

Thus, history with unresolved attribution cannot obtain a complete preservation result, even when its native content is complete.

**Minimum correction:** Distinguish these conditions:

- Ambiguous **dataset identity, dependency membership, or capture boundary** blocks completeness.
- Unknown or conflicting **historical account/project/parent attribution** remains explicit in the archive. It blocks only operations that require its resolution.

Preserve conflicting evidence without selecting an unsupported attribution.

**Decisive acceptance proof:** A complete conversation with unresolved account attribution can commit and restore with that uncertainty intact. An unresolved descendant or attachment still blocks completeness.

## Feasibility limits, not additional defects

The draft correctly leaves these capabilities unproved and fail-closed:

- Provider-wide closure and cross-component capture boundaries.
- Version-specific native restoration without private-format rewrites.
- Provider exclusion of late writes through removal.
- AIMeter acknowledgement through the exact final boundary.
- Origin-aware replay before live promotion.

For multi-origin history, the future acknowledgement interface must either cover each execution origin or refuse pruning. One source-host receipt cannot substitute for that proof.

The archive/source transaction split, permanent commit evidence, cleanup-family veto requirements, and bounded control path are coherent apart from finding 1. This review establishes no runtime completeness or native restoration result.

## Round 2 result

Read all 1,001 lines. The digest matches:

`979a1bc105bd9f9f359c708801106e2c787f5d8b9dbd6e094fa5c1b6d1d0a183`

**One high-severity design gap remains.** No edits or experiments occurred.

### High — External source dependencies lack durable cleanup-veto discovery

**Affected sections:** [6A: roles and protection](/Users/spencer/src/reap/docs/decisions/DEC-LIFETIME-AUTHORITY.md:264), [9: discovery](/Users/spencer/src/reap/docs/decisions/DEC-LIFETIME-AUTHORITY.md:716), and [11: exact scopes](/Users/spencer/src/reap/docs/decisions/DEC-LIFETIME-AUTHORITY.md:845).

**Trace:**

1. A native home carries `conversation_source` and an enabled archive obligation.
2. Its known alias points to shared history outside that home. The external container has no preservation-role declaration.
3. That container also falls under an ordinary store or ancestor disposal rule.
4. Reap restarts without inventory hints. A scoped cleanup evaluates the external container before archive discovery runs.
5. Fresh ancestor/descendant traversal finds no conversation-source role. The configured archive endpoint is elsewhere.
6. Generic cleanup can therefore select history whose separate native prune requirements have not passed.

Section 6A prohibits this outcome, but the discovery mechanism does not establish the off-tree dependency veto. Archive-job reservations protect only admitted work. Exact profile scope permits assessment; it does not itself supply durable lifetime protection.

**Minimum correction:**

Before activation, establish durable, discoverable protection at every canonical external history component. A co-located protective declaration on each applicable storage container is one simple route.

Alternatively, specify a complete dependency-veto mechanism for ordinary executors. It must survive cache loss and unavailable original homes. Unknown dependencies must block affected removal. Refuse activation where this protection cannot be established; do not rely on archive-first scheduling.

**Decisive acceptance proof:**

Use isolated fixtures with two alias homes and one external shared payload under an otherwise eligible store/ancestor rule. Remove hints and make the original homes unavailable. Run cleanup before archive discovery.

Every ordinary deletion family must preserve the shared payload, including Cargo-shaped content and explicit purge selection where applicable. Only the separately authorized native prune transaction may release covered units. An unrelated disposable sibling must remain removable.

This is a missing protection mechanism, not an unproved provider capability.

## Other reviewed boundaries

I found no additional blocking/high defect in committed-archive protection, durable publication/replay, independent retrieval, or prompt control. The draft now explicitly separates archive commit from source release and retains immutable archive evidence beyond job expiry.

Identity feasibility remains the first open gate. Native closure/restoration, provider-safe removal, AIMeter acknowledgement, resource limits, and runtime behavior remain unproved implementation gates. Review does not pass them.

**Recommendation:** Correct the external-component veto mechanism before design-stage acceptance. Parent retains final acceptance.

Read all 1,030 lines. The SHA-256 matches the supplied value.

**No blocking/high design finding remains in this lane. No medium issue requires correction before design acceptance.**

### Resolved findings

- **Off-tree source veto:** Resolved. Generic cleanup can find protection at the canonical history container without the alias home, configuration, or cache. Partial activation leaves protection in place without enabling archival or pruning. References carry no lifetime authority, so this does not introduce a second lifetime database. [Protection and activation](/Users/spencer/src/reap/docs/decisions/DEC-LIFETIME-AUTHORITY.md:271)
- **Unknown attribution:** Resolved. Unknown historical attribution can remain in a complete capture. Unknown dependency membership or capture boundaries still block completeness. [Closure distinction](/Users/spencer/src/reap/docs/decisions/DEC-LIFETIME-AUTHORITY.md:342)
- **Multi-origin consumption:** Resolved at the design level. A source-home receipt cannot substitute for every represented execution origin. Missing coverage blocks pruning, not preservation. [Origin coverage](/Users/spencer/src/reap/docs/decisions/DEC-LIFETIME-AUTHORITY.md:493)

### Additional adversarial review

The two self-review corrections withstand the concrete traces:

- A receiver cannot discard an incoming slot after uncertain publication or while its publisher survives. The exception cannot reach committed captures or neighboring slots. [Recovery exception](/Users/spencer/src/reap/docs/decisions/DEC-LIFETIME-AUTHORITY.md:460)
- A local same-volume capture cannot wait behind its own receiver: one worker performs both roles. Cross-volume dispatch requires the complete volume set. [Worker allocation](/Users/spencer/src/reap/docs/decisions/DEC-LIFETIME-AUTHORITY.md:518)

The combined rules also retain the important boundaries:

- Archive commit does not authorize source release.
- Job expiry cannot remove archive-local integrity or commit evidence.
- Legacy, purge, Cargo, and ancestor paths must enforce preservation vetoes.
- Slow capture, verification, and consumption work stays outside the control response path.

### Residual feasibility limits

Native closure, cross-component capture, isolated version-specific restoration, provider-safe removal, and AIMeter acknowledgements remain unproved. The draft refuses completeness or pruning when the relevant proof is absent. It does not invent a provider interface or require blind private-format edits.

**I am satisfied with this lane’s design review.** This conclusion does not establish runtime completeness, native restoration, or authority to activate or implement the design.

**No blocking/high finding remains in this lane. No medium issue requires correction before design acceptance.**

### Resolved findings

- **Off-tree source protection:** Resolved. In the prior failure trace, cleanup now encounters protection beside the external payload. Missing homes, configuration, or caches cannot remove that veto. Component references supply routing, not lifetime or prune authority. This does not introduce a second lifetime database.
- **Partial activation:** Resolved. Protective declarations precede activation. An interruption leaves protection in place without enabling archive/prune policy. Unsupported containers cause refusal.
- **Alias changes:** Resolved within the stated managed boundary. New components receive protection before reference publication. Cache omission cannot release old components. Arbitrary external relocation remains an explicit limitation.
- **Unpublished-slot recovery:** Resolved. Discard requires exact slot identity, durable ownership, no publication, and no surviving publisher. Uncertain publication blocks discard. This exception cannot remove a committed capture or another slot.
- **Same-volume receiver deadlock:** Resolved. One worker performs both roles. Cross-volume dispatch requires the complete volume set; remote preparation cannot wait with partial reservations.
- **Attribution and consumption:** Resolved. Unknown historical attribution need not block complete preservation. Source removal requires complete acknowledgement coverage from every represented execution origin.

### Combined-design assessment

The all-executor veto remains consistent across Cargo, legacy adapters, ancestor removal, explicit purge selectors, and recovery paths. Archive publication and source release remain separate transactions. Archive-local commit evidence survives job expiry and local-state loss.

I found no new contradiction that moves archive discovery, hashing, transfer, recovery, or consumer assessment onto the bounded response path.

**Design review is not runtime proof.** Identity feasibility remains the first open gate. Native capture/restoration, provider-safe removal, AIMeter acknowledgements, crash recovery, and resource/latency behavior remain unproved.
